findings.case: split_tag('fact','127.0.0.1:8080') and 'http://example.com:80/x' and 'ver 3.13:5' all return SRC
findings.why: Host:port, IP:port and version:number match the file:line pattern, so unverified facts get [SRC] instead of [ø].
Common real source pointers (GitHub #L9, 'line N') are not recognised, so these facts are under-tagged as unknown.

findings.case: item 'v1.2' met by message 'v1.2.3'; item 'port 8080' met by 'port 8080 is wrong'
findings.why: Lookaround uses \w, so '.' counts as a boundary. Prefix versions and negated or contradicting statements still satisfy the gate.

findings.case: item 'use py' vs confirmed claim 'Use py.' returns False
findings.why: Exact match after norm ignores trailing punctuation, so a legitimate confirmed claim with a final period does not meet the requires item.
Whole-phrase match still counts negated or incidental mentions as 'stated'; the negation false-positive the fix claims to remove remains for short items.

findings.case: requires ['port 8080'], confirmed claim 'Port 8080.' (trailing period), message '' -> False
findings.why: Exact normalised equality is brittle: punctuation or wording differences leave a genuinely confirmed claim unmet, so the skill never loads.
Host:port or IP:port evidence matches the file:line regex; untagged facts are falsely promoted to [SRC].
Pointers to extensionless files (Makefile, Dockerfile, LICENSE) are rejected, so a legitimately seen-in-source fact is tagged [ø].
